historical_reviews.deepseek: The sequence has no valid idle baseline and cannot show the fan response curve because stress is already active when the first RPM snapshot is labeled idle.

historical_reviews.history: Exact-code/source search found no earlier V3.1 record for this identity.
historical_reviews.v3_1: Automatic fan control normally responds to temperature and policy hysteresis rather than CPU utilization directly. Power can rise immediately while RPM changes only after sensors cross a threshold, so synchronized workload, power, temperature and RPM curves plus stabilization criteria are required instead of a single monotonic before/after check.

original_test_intent: Verify that the platform's unchanged automatic fan-control policy raises cooling response appropriately when a controlled full-load condition increases system power and thermal demand relative to a stable idle baseline.
original_method: Pin the fan policy, fan/power/temperature sensor map and approved workload, reach a defined idle steady state, capture multiple synchronized samples, run a bounded full-system stress with workload/thermal/power aborts and guaranteed cleanup, sample throughout ramp/steady/cooldown, and compare policy-aware response latency and magnitude without writing fan controls.
manual_activity: A platform/thermal owner approves the full-load profile, fan policy, sensor mappings, response/hysteresis expectations and abort limits and decides the verdict.
required_inputs: Approved CPU/system stress profile and duration
safety_requirements: Confirm automatic mode before and after
Do not change fan curves, duty or power policy
Stop and clean up on sensor error or limit excursion
Do not retry blindly after thermal events
agent_execution_scope: Launch only the approved bounded stress
Continuously capture workload, fan, power and temperature

command_applicability.original_deepseek_command_fit: It uses relevant tools but starts stress before the baseline, mislabels an in-load snapshot as idle, truncates sensors and captures no during-load power/RPM/temperature series or cleanup proof.
command_applicability.command_recommendation: Capture a stable multi-sample idle baseline, run the approved bounded stress with continuous complete telemetry and abort controls, then prove process cleanup, cooldown and unchanged automatic mode.
command_applicability.original_parameters_and_time_preserved: Idle-to-stress comparison and 6-minute activity remain; the exact full-load profile and necessary stabilization intervals require owner approval rather than the unsourced 30-second CPU load.

modernized_recommendation.recommended_method: Plot aligned workload, power, inlet/component temperature and every fan RPM across idle, ramp, steady load and cooldown, then evaluate policy threshold, latency and stable range.
modernized_recommendation.difference_from_original_method: Replaces two ambiguous snapshots with a causal, time-aligned response curve under unchanged automatic control.
modernized_recommendation.coverage_difference: Power can increase without immediate RPM change, and a late or hysteretic but correct fan response would fail a simplistic snapshot while a preloaded baseline could falsely pass.
modernized_recommendation.risks_limitations: CPU-only stress may not represent full-system thermal demand; the owner must define which resources and duration constitute full load for this platform.

project_override_considerations: Define idle stability, full-load resources/utilization/duration, sensor sources, sampling interval, expected power increase, automatic-control threshold/latency/RPM response, hysteresis, temperature/power aborts and cooldown completion.
expected_evidence: Workload drain, tool versions and exact bounded command
Complete raw idle/load/cooldown fan/power/temperature time series
Stress stdout/stderr, exit status and cleanup proof
Preserved logs, unchanged auto mode, safety audit and engineer verdict

source_conflict_analysis.analysis: Items, Procedure and Criteria consistently request automatic fan/power response from idle to load. The simplistic monotonic criterion requires project-specific policy detail but does not contradict the intent.

blocked_analysis.analysis: Stress profile, sensor mapping and control policy are identifiable inputs. Execution becomes BLOCKED if a safe bounded load or authoritative fan-response policy cannot be established.

review_improvement: Turns an invalidly ordered sparse command into a safe causal response test that separates power rise, thermal lag and fan-policy behavior.
independent_technical_reasoning: Automatic fans react to thermal sensors through thresholds, filters and hysteresis, not directly to the stress process. The evidence must therefore show the causal chain from workload to power/temperature to RPM over time; comparing one pre/post value cannot distinguish correct delayed control from missing response or a mislabeled baseline.
